## Setting up the graph

A 2-element subset $\{i,j\}$ with $i<j$ corresponds to the lattice point $(i,j)$. Moving one token one step along the path changes exactly one coordinate by $\pm 1$. The only forbidden move is one that makes the two tokens coincide, i.e., leaving the region $1\le i<j\le n$.

So $T_2(P_n)$ is the induced grid subgraph of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ on the staircase region
$$R_n=\{(i,j): 1\le i<j\le n\},\qquad |R_n|=\binom{n}{2}\sim \frac{n^2}{2}.$$

## Lower bound

In the grid $\mathbb{Z}^2$, a closed neighborhood has at most 5 vertices, so each vertex of $T_2(P_n)$ dominates at most 5 vertices. Hence
$$\gamma(T_2(P_n))\ \ge\ \frac{|R_n|}{5}\ \sim\ \frac{n^2}{10}.$$

## Upper bound

The infinite grid has a perfect dominating set (a perfect code) of density $1/5$, for example $\{(x,y): x+2y\equiv 0 \pmod 5\}$. Restrict this pattern to $R_n$. Every vertex of $R_n$ whose dominator lies inside $R_n$ is dominated. The only undominated vertices are those whose perfect-code dominator falls outside $R_n$. These lie within distance 1 of the boundary of $R_n$: the diagonal $i=j-1$ and the outer edges $i=1$, $j=n$. There are $O(n)$ such vertices, and adding each of them to the set costs $O(n)$ additional vertices. Therefore
$$\gamma(T_2(P_n))\ \le\ \frac{n^2}{10}+O(n).$$

## Conclusion

Combining the bounds,
$$\gamma(T_2(P_n)) = \frac{n^2}{10}+O(n),$$
so
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\gamma(T_2(P_n))}{n^2}=\frac{1}{10}.$$

ANSWER: 1/10
